occurrences.insertion: Ulnar side of the adjacent metacarpal.

occurrences.name: Intermetacarpales
occurrences.note: Lizards often have four 'intermetacarpales I'.

occurrences.name: Intermetacarpales
occurrences.note: Part of the interossei dorsales sensu Meers (2003).
occurrences.attachmentNote: Meers's crocodylian names are bridged to this record through Abdala & Diogo's Table 1, which gives the Caiman column with explicit 'sensu Meers, 2003' equivalences. = part of Mm. interossei dorsalae. M. interosseus dorsalis digiti II runs from the dorsomedial surface of metacarpal I, just distal to the deep extensor origins of digits I and II, onto the lateral surface of the metacarpophalangeal joint of digit II and the lateral distal third of metacarpal II. **Abdala & Diogo split Meers's interossei dorsalae between this record and the dorsometacarpales without saying which slips go where**, so the same rows sit on both and neither should be read as the whole complex.

occurrences.name: Interossei (partim)
occurrences.note: Rattus norvegicus, from Abdala & Diogo's Tables 2-3. Contributes, with the flexores breves profundi, to the mammalian interossei.

occurrences.name: Intermetacarpales
occurrences.note: Zaglossus bruijnii. Absent in Tachyglossidae. Gambaryan et al. report this against Kajava (1911) and Howell (1936), who had it the other way round — present in echidnas and absent in the platypus.

occurrences.name: Intermetacarpales
occurrences.note: Tachyglossus aculeatus. Absent, against Kajava (1911) and Howell (1936). A sourced absence in one genus of a clade whose other genus has the muscle, which is what makes Monotremata compute as `variable` here rather than as present.

occurrences.name: Intermetacarpales
occurrences.origin: Four muscles: the first from the postaxial side of metacarpal II, the second from the preaxial side of metacarpal III, the third from the postaxial side of metacarpal III, the fourth from the preaxial side of metacarpal IV — two in the space between metacarpals II and III, two between III and IV.
occurrences.insertion: Each is unipennate, its fibres inserting on a tendon parallel to the metacarpal of origin which runs along the same digit to end at the tip of phalanx 1, on the same side as the origin. Digit II therefore carries a postaxial muscle, digit IV a preaxial one, and digit III both.
occurrences.attachmentNote: Ornithorhynchus anatinus. = mm. interossei dorsales. Present here and absent in both echidnas, which Gambaryan et al. count among the ways the platypus is the more primitive monotreme below the elbow.

occurrences.name: Interossei
occurrences.note:
Tawa hallae. Scored present and given no attachment rows on purpose. Burch (2014) treats the Interossei as almost certainly present in the manus of *Tawa*, on their presence in some form in every other tetrapod, but impossible to reconstruct with confidence: there is no consistency in their number or morphology across his study taxa, and — unusually for this reconstruction, which leans hard on osteology — **no osteological correlates in *Tawa*'s metacarpals** for any of the possible attachment sites. The avian evidence cannot help: both muscles birds call 'Interosseus' are of uncertain homology with the interossei of other tetrapods on both attachments and development (Sullivan 1962), and Howell (1936) had already found the relationship between Interossei, Intermetacarpales, Dorsometacarpales and Contrahentes digitorum unclear among tetrapods generally. Which of this dataset's records Burch's Interossei map onto is therefore left open, and the same note is filed on [[dorsometacarpales]].

What he will say is what the crocodylian arrangement would have bought: an abductor (dorsal) and an adductor (ventral) for each digit, both from the proximal end of the adjacent metacarpal to the distal metacarpal, joint capsule and/or proximal phalanx of their own — independent adduction and abduction of each finger, not unlike the human hand.

Homo sapiens, Gest (Anatomy Tables). The human dorsal and palmar interossei are scored on [[flexores-breves-profundi]], whose synonymy already claims them. This record's synonymy claims them too — 'part of interossei dorsales' — and Howell (1936) found the relationship between Interossei, Intermetacarpales, Dorsometacarpales and Contrahentes digitorum unclear across tetrapods generally. Scored uncertain rather than duplicating the attachment rows onto a second record, which would give one observation two homes.

homology.notes: Universal. The persistent difficulty is the boundary with the flexores breves profundi in taxa where authors lump both as 'interossei'.

muscles.name: Dorsometacarpales
muscles.developmental: Somitic; dorsal intrinsic layer of the manus.

consensus.origin: Dorsal surfaces of the metacarpals.
consensus.insertion: Dorsal aponeuroses and proximal phalanges.
consensus.action: Extend and spread the digits.

occurrences.note: Marked '– [see text]'.

occurrences.name: Dorsometacarpales
occurrences.attachmentNote: Trachemys scripta, from Walker (1973). His Mm. interossei dorsales: from the distal carpals and metacarpals, deep to the extensores digitorum breves, running distally along the top and side of each digit onto the individual phalanges. Unlike the breves they stay typical even where the breves are reduced — they are present and normal in Pelomedusa, which has lost all but one of the breves.

occurrences.name: Dorsometacarpales
occurrences.attachmentNote: Meers's crocodylian names are bridged to this record through Abdala & Diogo's Table 1, which gives the Caiman column with explicit 'sensu Meers, 2003' equivalences. = part of Mm. interossei dorsalae, the other half of the split described on the intermetacarpales. Abdala & Diogo assign this record and the intermetacarpales each to 'part of' Meers's interossei dorsalae without resolving the division, so these rows describe the complex rather than this record alone.

occurrences.name: Interossei
occurrences.note: Tawa hallae. Scored present and given no attachment rows on purpose; see the matching row on [[intermetacarpales]] for the reasoning. Burch (2014) reconstructs the Interossei as present but unreconstructable — no consistency across taxa, no osteological correlates on *Tawa*'s metacarpals, and an avian pair whose homology with the tetrapod interossei is uncertain. The dorsal set of the crocodylian arrangement he describes — an abductor per digit from the proximal end of the adjacent metacarpal — is the part that would land on this record if the mapping were settled.

Homo sapiens, Gest (Anatomy Tables). As for [[intermetacarpales]]: the human interossei are scored once, on [[flexores-breves-profundi]], and this record's claim on them is recorded rather than acted on. Burch's *Tawa* row here is uncertain for a different reason — the muscles are almost certainly present but leave no osteological correlate to reconstruct from.

homology.notes: The dorsal counterpart of the intermetacarpales. Frequently subsumed into 'interossei dorsales' by authors who do not separate dorsal from ventral intrinsic layers.

muscles.name: Abductor pollicis brevis
muscles.developmental: Somitic; ventral intrinsic layer of the manus.
synonyms: abductor alulae / abductor indicis (birds — Meyers 1996; Sullivan 1962; Shellswell & Wolpert 1977)

consensus.origin: Radial carpals and the flexor retinaculum.
consensus.insertion: Base of the proximal phalanx of the most radial digit.
consensus.action: Abducts the most radial digit.

occurrences.note: Seemingly absent in Ambystoma ordinarium.

occurrences.name: Abductor pollicis brevis
occurrences.note: Ribbing (1907) held that Gaupp's (1896) 'abductor pollicis' is the pronator quadratus, not this muscle.
occurrences.attachmentNote: In anurans the preaxial muscles serve the PREPOLLEX, not digit 1 — the adductor pollicis arises tendinously from distal carpal 3-4-5 and inserts on the palmar and distal prepollex. Digit 1 is absent, and the muscles that would serve it attach to the preaxial element instead.

occurrences.name: Abductor pollicis brevis
occurrences.note: = abductor metacarpi I sensu Meers (2003).
occurrences.attachmentNote: Meers's crocodylian names are bridged to this record through Abdala & Diogo's Table 1, which gives the Caiman column with explicit 'sensu Meers, 2003' equivalences. = M. abductor metacarpi I. Fleshy from the ventrolateral surface of the radiale, by a stout tendon onto the proximolateral base of metacarpal I.

occurrences.name: Abductor alulae
occurrences.note: The 'abductor alulae' sensu Meyers (1996) corresponds to the 'abductor indicis' sensu Sullivan (1962) and goes to digit 1 (= digit 2 according to embryology) — so it seemingly corresponds to the abductor pollicis brevis.

occurrences.name: Abductor pollicis brevis
occurrences.innervation: Recurrent branch of the median nerve.
occurrences.attachmentNote: Galictis cuja. Abductor digiti I brevis, from the distal margin of the radial sesamoid onto the medial surface of the proximal end of the proximal phalanx of digit I, sometimes with an extra fleshy insertion on the ventromedial metacarpal I. A muscle whose origin is a sesamoid rather than a bone of the carpus.

occurrences.name: Abductor pollicis brevis
occurrences.action: Abducts the first digit.
occurrences.attachmentNote:
Tawa hallae, Burch (2014). The avian homolog is Abductor alulae. **The origin is the most variable attachment in the manus**: the ventral radiale in all crocodylians, most lepidosaurs and one turtle (*Lissemys*); the distal carpals in *Trachemys* and *Tetradactylus*; the distal radius in *Podocnemis* and *Trachemys*; the base of the carpometacarpus in some birds; the extensor carpi radialis tendon in most birds; and a variable accessory attachment to the distal radius in *Struthio*. Presence in most lepidosaurs and in crocodylians makes the radiale plesiomorphic at 0.881 at the base of Archosauria, and it is scored here as the state a basal theropod is unlikely to have exchanged for the derived avian one — but it remains phylogenetically equivocal.

The insertion is not: the medial surface of the first phalanx of digit I near its base, at 0.837 at Archosauria and 0.993 at Aves. The more proximal insertion on the lateral aspect of metacarpal I found in crocodylians (Meers 2003), *Sphenodon* (Miner 1925) and *Liolaemus* is the state Burch does not take, against the usual pull of the crocodylian half of the bracket.

occurrences.name: Abductor pollicis brevis
occurrences.action: Abducts the thumb.
occurrences.innervation: Recurrent branch of the median nerve.
occurrences.attachmentNote: Homo sapiens, Gest (Anatomy Tables). Flexor retinaculum, scaphoid and trapezium, to the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb. The distal insertion — on the phalanx rather than on metacarpal I — is the state found in turtles, most lepidosaurs and all birds, and reconstructed for *Tawa* at 0.837; crocodylians, *Sphenodon* and *Liolaemus* keep the more proximal metacarpal insertion. **The origin is the variable end** across every clade this record holds, and the human version adds a retinaculum the outgroups do not have. Scaphoid and trapezium are scored as `carpals` and `distal-carpals`; naming them as elements would create two bones for one species.

homology.notes: Present in nearly all columns. The avian case is entangled with the unresolved bird digit-identity problem: the muscle goes to the digit that is 1 by position but 2 by embryology.

muscles.name: Abductor digiti minimi
muscles.developmental: Somitic; ventral intrinsic layer of the manus.
synonyms: abductor digitorum V (Abdala et al. 2008; Abdala & Moro 2006)

consensus.origin: Ulnar carpals (pisiform) and the flexor retinaculum.
consensus.insertion: Base of the proximal phalanx of the most ulnar digit.
consensus.action: Abducts the most ulnar digit.

occurrences.name: Abductor digiti minimi
occurrences.note: In Taricha and Ambystoma the muscle attaches to digit 4 because digit 5 is absent — the ulnar counterpart of the anuran abductor pollicis longus case. The muscle finds the most ulnar digit available.
occurrences.attachmentNote: Recorded as m. extensor lateralis digiti IV. It serves digit IV because digit V is absent from the salamander manus — the same postaxial position as the amniote abductor digiti minimi on digit V, one digit over. A case where matching by digit number and matching by position give different answers.
occurrences.origin: Ulnare and intermedium.
occurrences.insertion: Lateral edge of the fourth metacarpal.

occurrences.name: Abductor digiti minimi
occurrences.note: Attachment rows for this taxon describe the foot and have been moved to the pes record.

occurrences.name: Abductor digiti minimi
occurrences.attachmentNote: Scored from Zaaf et al.'s tables for Eublepharis macularius, with the Gekko gecko differences noted where they bear on the attachment. From the ulnare along the whole length of the ulnar edge of metacarpal V.

occurrences.name: Abductor digiti minimi
occurrences.attachmentNote: Alligator and Crocodylus, from Meers's descriptions. M. abductor metacarpi V, by fleshy attachment to the distal surface of the pisiform just distal to the insertion of flexor carpi ulnaris, inserting tendinously along the lateral surface of metacarpal V.

occurrences.note: Absent in chickens even though a most-ulnar digit is present. Abdala & Diogo treat this as the counter-case: here the specific IDENTITY of the digit (3 by fossils and Hox, 4 by embryology) seems to matter, not merely its position. They flag it as an open problem.

occurrences.name: Abductor digiti minimi
occurrences.innervation: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve.
occurrences.attachmentNote: Galictis cuja. Abductor digiti V, from the distal surface of the accessory carpal in two bellies: the medial onto the lateral sesamoid of digit V, the lateral onto the digit itself.

occurrences.name: Abductor digiti minimi
occurrences.attachmentNote: Gekko gecko, from the differences column of Zaaf et al.'s tables. Zaaf et al. examined this muscle in both geckos and record no difference, so the Eublepharis rows stand for Gekko too. A blank in a differences column is an observation of sameness, not a gap, and scoring it as a row is what lets the clade rollup say the two species AGREE rather than say nothing.

occurrences.name: Abductor digiti minimi
occurrences.action: Abducts the fourth digit and the manus.
occurrences.attachmentNote:
Tawa hallae, Burch (2014). **This row exists because Burch dissected two ostriches.** No muscle answering to this description had ever been reported in the avian manus, which would leave the archosaur bracket one-sided; he found a well-developed one in both *Struthio* specimens, arising from the ventral surface of the pseudoulnare and the flexor carpi ulnaris insertion tendon and inserting on the ventrolateral surface of metacarpal III. Since muscles that attached to the pisiform have shifted to the pseudoulnare in birds, that origin is treated as homologous with the pisiform origin of crocodylians, lizards and turtles, and the bracket closes.

Burch also rejects Diogo & Abdala's (2010) alternative homolog for this muscle, the avian Ulnimetacarpalis dorsalis, on development: that muscle belongs to the dorsal division with the short extensors, while abductor digiti minimi is a ventral muscle described by some authors as part of flexor carpi ulnaris or as arising from its insertion tendon. In *Tawa* it arises from the pisiform, which is still present, and inserts on the metacarpal of the reduced fourth digit — a lateralmost-metacarpal insertion like the crocodylian one, which may itself be a consequence of lateral digit reduction in both extant clades.

occurrences.name: Abductor digiti minimi
occurrences.action: Abducts the fifth digit.
occurrences.innervation: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve.
occurrences.attachmentNote: Homo sapiens, Gest (Anatomy Tables). Pisiform to the ulnar side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the fifth digit — the same origin crocodylians, lizards and turtles use, and the same phalangeal insertion lepidosaurs and turtles use rather than the crocodylian metacarpal one. **The pisiform is what makes this row possible**, and it is the bone birds lost: Burch found the muscle in *Struthio* only because it had relocated to the neomorphic pseudoulnare, which was the first report of it in an avian manus. A human keeps the plesiomorphic arrangement intact.

homology.notes: The muscle's homology is secure; the interest is entirely in which digit it lands on. Urodeles: digit 4 (positional). Birds: absent despite an available digit (identity-dependent). These two cells are the crux of Abdala & Diogo's position-versus-identity argument.
homology.openQuestion: Why is the abductor digiti minimi absent in chickens when the most ulnar digit is present? Resolution depends on the unsettled bird digit-identity question.
homology.teaching: Teach this cell together with the anuran abductor pollicis longus. The pair sets up position-based attachment; the bird cell breaks it. That tension is the lesson.

muscles.name: Extensor digitorum profundus
synonyms: extensor pollicis et indicis (Gambaryan et al. 2015)
extensor pollicis longus + extensor indicis + extensor digitus III proprius (Diogo & Abdala 2010)

consensus.origin: Anterior (dorsal) surface of the ulna.
consensus.insertion: Ungual phalanges, preaxial and proximal to the corresponding branches of the extensor digitorum.
consensus.action: Extends the terminal phalanges.

occurrences.name: Extensor pollicis et indicis
occurrences.origin: Anterior surface of the ulna except its distal end and the olecranon, with a small tubercle at the proximal point of the area of origin.
occurrences.insertion: A flat tendon, formed as a superficial aponeurosis over the distal two-thirds of the belly, passing under the retinaculum extensorum deeper than the extensor digitorum communis tendon and separated from it by a bridge of that retinaculum, then splitting into three branches to the ungual phalanges of digits II-IV, each preaxial and proximal to the corresponding extensor digitorum branch.
occurrences.attachmentNote: Zaglossus bruijnii. Digits II-IV here, I-IV in Tachyglossus and I-III in the platypus; Gambaryan et al. read the four-digit condition as the most primitive of the three. Scored here from Monotremata only; the muscle is not yet scored in other taxa in this dataset, so its absence elsewhere is unsampled rather than observed.
occurrences.divisionNote: Undivided, and its integrity is listed among the primitive monotreme features. Placentals usually split it into the extensor pollicis longus and the extensor indicis, the latter often keeping a tendon to digit III and sometimes IV.

occurrences.name: Extensor pollicis et indicis
occurrences.origin: Anterior surface of the ulna, excluding its distal end but including the base of the olecranon; the belly also receives a small bundle of fibres from the extensor digitorum communis.
occurrences.insertion: Branches to the ungual phalanges of digits II-IV as in the long-beaked echidna, plus a branch to the ungual phalanx of digit I which joins the corresponding extensor digitorum communis tendon at its insertion; before dividing, the ventral surface of the common tendinous plate also sends deeper branches to the bases of the preungual phalanges of digits II-IV.
occurrences.attachmentNote: Tachyglossus aculeatus. The four-digit formula Gambaryan et al. take as primitive, and the only one of the three with the extra collateral insertions onto the preungual phalanges. Scored here from Monotremata only; the muscle is not yet scored in other taxa in this dataset, so its absence elsewhere is unsampled rather than observed.

occurrences.name: Extensor pollicis et indicis
occurrences.origin: Mainly the olecranon: the origin descends from its anterior projection along the anterior side of the ulnar crest to the level of the elbow joint and a little beyond.
occurrences.insertion: A flat tendon over the distal half of the belly, passing under the retinaculum extensorum deeper than the extensor digitorum communis tendon and splitting into three branches to the ungual phalanges of digits I-III, shared with the corresponding extensor digitorum communis branches.
occurrences.attachmentNote: Ornithorhynchus anatinus. The origin has withdrawn onto the olecranon, off the ulnar shaft the echidnas use, and the digital formula has shifted preaxially — I-III rather than II-IV. Scored here from Monotremata only; the muscle is not yet scored in other taxa in this dataset, so its absence elsewhere is unsampled rather than observed.

occurrences.name: Extensor pollicis longus and extensor indicis
occurrences.action: Extends the thumb at the interphalangeal joint and the index finger at all three joints.
occurrences.innervation: Deep branch of the radial nerve.
occurrences.attachmentNote: Homo sapiens, Gest (Anatomy Tables). Extensor pollicis longus from the interosseous membrane and the middle posterolateral ulna to the base of the distal phalanx of the thumb; extensor indicis from the membrane and the distal ulna, joining the extensor digitorum tendon to digit II. **These are the two muscles Diogo & Abdala use to define this record**, which exists to hold the deep dorsal antebrachial layer that turtles and lepidosaurs also have and that the superficial extensor digitorum obscures. The third member of their set, extensor digiti III proprius, is not present in a human.

homology.notes: A deep digital extensor distinct from the extensor digitorum, arising from the ulna rather than the humerus. Haines (1939) named it the extensor digitorum profundus; Diogo & Abdala (2010) carry it in therians as three muscles — extensor pollicis longus, extensor indicis and extensor digitus III proprius — and Gambaryan et al. (2015) find it undivided in monotremes and count that integrity among the primitive features. **Scored so far only in Monotremata, so its absence elsewhere in this dataset is unsampled rather than observed** — the record exists because there was nowhere to put a muscle three sources agree on, not because monotremes are the only animals with one.
homology.openQuestion: Is the therian three-way split of this muscle one event or three, and does the extensor indicis retain the tendon to digit III (and sometimes IV) because it is the unsplit remnant?
